items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: Yeah, Louie Kepard. He was the fellow that played a guitar.

ctx.x: This is Roy Palmer speaking, and I want to say about the bands, different bands that we have played with in the Orleans and in different towns, different places. I want to explain how I came along in the music game. It was when I was around 15 or 18, I studied music, taking music. From that time I was taking bands, taking bands. I played with regular, and sometimes I played with other bands. I led a lot of bands, bass band and so on. My music was well established because I played and I played with other bands. I…

a very good band. What did they pay in the parades? In the parades they paid two dollars an hour. Yes, two dollars an hour. They only paraded about two hours and a half. We only made about four or five hours on the parade. We had so many different, and then through Connerville, and like those days, well we got hired. We had to play probably six or eight hours we played, see? Or eight or ten hours at night, see? For dances? Yeah, for dances, see? Different places at the fairground and at the Louisiana Park, and…

items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1961-01-19
items.q: Well, Roy Palmer, he was playing with, when I first got him, he was playing with Amos Raleigh.

ctx.x: Chicago girl now. See? See that? Is there anything about Roy Palmer that you can tell us?

Well, Roy Palmer, he was playing with, when I first got him, he was playing with Amos Raleigh. You know who I talk about Amos Raleigh? Yes. A corn-ed player. Well, he used to be with that, I believe if I'm mistaken, it was the Tulane Band. The Tulane Band. That was Amos Raleigh. He was a corn-ed player. Well, Amos, this fellow used to play with him. And, uh, this other fellow, what's the name again? He used to play tram on wood, him. And then he started going, he went to wood too. Well, I found it out and I don't…
No, he's still living. I saw him last year.

items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1957-08-04
items.q: I want to ask about this band, the one picture you have with Roy Palmer and Lawrence Dewey and Sugar Johnny.

ctx.x: Oakland right where Crozac is. Dates have their back entrance that Hall is given back there. Old man Umpra used to play with dear with Tick Chambers. You heard to talk about Tick Chambers? Yes, the Oakland Well, Tickshaber was playing cornet, and this fellow, Lawrence Dewitt, was playing clarinet at that time with him. And the old man, Umpra, was playing cyborg, clarinet over there with him also. Well, after he left, well, and the district closed down, well, they all reopened up with this fellow, little Willie…

You know, the rest of it. You know, it's just like, yeah, you see that voice note? Just like I said, well, I'm going to play in E-flat. All right, that voice note. Well, all the rest of the modern keys will follow right behind the system, brother. See? And every time they change, you can hear change, and in you lose. Is that going on here? Yes. Yes. I want to ask about this band, the one picture you have with Roy Palmer and Lawrence Dewey and Sugar Johnny. Yes, well, I'll tell you.
